notes: `reports/VerificationTasks.pdf` section 10.1, Task 7: verify `Q↑ ⊆ Q` under the views `Va`, `Vb`, `Vc`. Global schema `{F}` (ternary), where `F(x, y, u)` is a non-stop flight from airport `x` to airport `y` on airline `u`; constants `"a"`, `"b"`, `"c"`. Local schema `{Va, Vb, Vc}` with the conjunctive views `Va(x, y) ↔ F(x, y, "a")`, `Vb(y, u) ↔ F("b", y, u)` and `Vc(x, z) ↔ ∃y. F(x, y, "c") ∧ F(y, z, "c")`.

The source documents the reformulations task document (sha256 `32a3ac6b428d851f0aaa4fb7acdbf2fe4ad5dacca93ee118837888ff91b7a1c6`) and `reports/VerificationTasks.pdf` (sha256 `796ff97c082c6fc70e75a60c0dd40ec0680b738d7184a8b8aefea8c681b3ebff`) carry the same section 10.1 text, so both name this task.

The command is not hand-authored: `Fidelity/Example4036.lean` states the PDF's Datalog programs, compiles each with `Datalog.WhielCompiler.Naive`, writes the two compiled commands one after the other, renames the generated snapshots `T_1`, `Q_1` and `QUp_1` to the auxiliary input names `T_aux`, `Q_aux` and `QUp_aux`, and proves the result equal to `inputCmd` by `decide +kernel`; the same module fixes `inputPre` as the three view equations and `inputPost` as the claim `QUp ⊆ Q` and pins the single loop `Hoare.preprocess` computes from the sequence.

Expected verdict valid. Every `QUp` rule unfolds to a same-airline itinerary out of `"b"`, so `QUp ⊆ Q`; no distinctness of the constants is assumed. The classification stays `unknown` because this corpus carries no certificate.

Reference encoding for intent only: `Benchmark/Example4036/Input.lean` on `origin/reformulation-multiview` at commit `7b793fe36c02d051a0771d110333d1c9bbca40cd`, an `IndexAlphaName` hand-written input in the earlier single-level framework whose precondition states the views as bi-inclusions. Nothing is copied from it.
The PDF's rule is `Q(y) :- T("b", y, u)` although its prose says the airports reachable "from a"; the rule is encoded literally, with the constant "b".
title: Airline reachability query versus its three-view reformulation, forward containment
explanation: The global program computes per-airline reachability T over a ternary flight relation F(x,y,u) (non-stop flight from x to y on airline u), then restricts to Q(y):-T("b",y,u), the airports reachable from "b" while staying on a single airline. The local reformulation QUp is built, without recursion, from three conjunctive views: Va (direct flights on airline "a"), Vb (flights out of "b"), and Vc (two-hop connections on airline "c"), combined by three rules. The Hoare triple claims a one-directional (forward) containment, QUp ⊆ Q: every airport the reformulation derives is genuinely reachable from "b" on one airline. Expected valid, since each QUp rule unfolds to a genuine same-airline itinerary out of "b"; no certificate exists yet, so the classification stays unknown. This case is the twin of Example4037, which tests the reverse direction of the same containment.
preInWords: The precondition states the three view equations: Va is F restricted to airline "a", Vb is F restricted to flights departing "b", and Vc is the two-hop composition of two airline-"c" flights.
postInWords: The postcondition asserts QUp ⊆ Q, that every airport reached by the three-view reformulation is reached by the global per-airline query.
